ops.text: 2026-07-17 RESOLVED. The DERP fallback was NOT host-side and NOT a missing passthrough config. Real root cause: the AT&T BGW320-505 had a **Fixed DHCP Allocation** (ipalloc.ha) binding the eero's WAN MAC 24:2d:6c:9a:4e:83 → private 192.168.1.64, which shadowed the already-correct IP Passthrough (ippass.ha: allocmode=passthrough, passmode=dhcps-fixed, MAC=eero, set 6+ months). Every eero reboot re-took the reserved private lease before passthrough could hand it the public IP → permanent double NAT (traceroute hop2=192.168.1.254) → no inbound UDP → all exit traffic on DERP. A BGW *reboot* would NOT have fixed it (reservation is persistent config). Fix executed: logged into BGW admin via cookiesync-free direct login (GET login.ha nonce → POST hashpassword=md5(deviceAccessCode+nonce), password field=N stars; 302→home.ha=success; lockout on repeated failures so ONE attempt/phase), then ipalloc.ha two-step (POST ConnHost_1_1=Allocate → GET → POST alloc_1_1=normal+Save) to convert the eero from Fixed Allocation to DHCP pool. Non-disruptive (eero kept .64 lease until reboot). Armed a local detached self-repair watchdog (PID reparented to launchd) that probes internet 20s and auto-restores a private reservation (tier1) / BGW-restart (tier2) on sustained outage — needed 0 reverts. User rebooted the eero (eero app); ~59s outage; eero re-DISCOVERed and passthrough handed it the public 104.1.90.148 (BGW devices.ha + host netmap now show eero=104.1.90.148, host advertises 104.1.90.148:41641). Verified DIRECT both ways: laptop→yasyf-home `via 104.1.90.148:41641` 161ms (was DERP sfo), host→laptop `via 27.123.186.170:41641`; status laptop CurAddr now non-empty (was empty/relay). Fleet unaffected (metal direct via vmnet 192.168.64.11). Note BGW passthrough is not a pure bridge (hop2 still 192.168.1.254) but the 2nd NAT is gone, which is what mattered. Watchdog disarmed, device access code + cookie jars shredded. Still open: en0 wired restore (Phase 4).
